blocks.name: Real World Example: Changes to Demand That Increase Price

blocks.text: Real World Example: Changes to Demand That Increase Price

blocks.md:
- **Real world markets** are constantly changing and are referred to as **dynamic markets**
- **Market equilibrium **can change every few minutes in some markets (e.g. stocks and shares), or every few weeks or months in others (e.g clothing)
- Any change to a **non-price determinant of demand or supply** will temporarily create **disequilibrium **and market forces will then seek to clear the **excess demand or supply**
- During lock downs associated with the Covid-19 pandemic, furniture retailers experienced **unexpectedly high demand** for their products (especially desks and sofas)

blocks.text: Diagram: Increase in Demand for Desks

blocks.alt: An increase in demand for desks due to a temporary change in tastes/fashions

blocks.md: ***An increase in demand for desks due to a temporary change in tastes/fashions***

- Due to the Covid mandated change of **working from home**, consumers experienced a temporary **change in taste** as they sought to **set up** comfortable **home offices**

  - This led to an **increase in demand** for desks from D<sub>1 </sub>→ D<sub>2 </sub>
- At the **original** market clearing price of P<sub>1</sub>, a condition of** excess demand **now exists

  - The demand for desks is **greater** than the supply
- In response, suppliers **raise prices**

  - This causes a **contraction of demand** and an **extension of supply** leading to a **new market equilibrium** at P<sub>2</sub>Q<sub>2</sub>
  - Both the **equilibrium price (P**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** and the **equilibrium quantity (Q**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** are higher than before
  - The **excess demand** in the market has been cleared

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: Be systematic in thinking through the order of changes in market conditions. E.g. An increase in demand (shift in demand) will cause a rise in price. The higher price will cause a movement along the supply curve (not a shift of supply)

blocks.name: Real World Example: Changes to Supply That Increase Price

blocks.text: Real World Example: Changes to Supply That Increase Price

blocks.md: - In September 2022, **Hurricane Fiona** destroyed much of Puerto Rico's crop of plantains (a necessity in the diet of local people)

blocks.alt: Decrease in supply of plantains in Puerto Rico due to a supply shock caused by Hurricane Fiona

blocks.md: ***Decrease in supply of plantains in Puerto Rico due to a supply shock caused by Hurricane Fiona***

- Due to Hurricane Fiona, Puerto Rico is experiencing a ***supply shock*** in its plantain market

  - This causes a **decrease in supply **of S<sub>1 </sub>→ S<sub>2</sub>
- At the **original** market clearing price of P<sub>1</sub>, a condition of** excess demand **now exists (shortage)

  - The demand for plantain is **greater** than the supply
- In response, sellers in Puerto Rico **raised prices**

  - This causes a **contraction of demand** and an **extension of supply,** leading to a **new market equilibrium** at **P**<sub>**2**</sub>**Q**<sub>**2**</sub>
  - The **equilibrium price (P**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** is higher and the e**quilibrium quantity (Q**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** is lower than before
  - The **excess demand** in the market has been cleared

blocks.name: Real World Example: Changes to Demand That Decrease Price

blocks.text: Real World Example: Changes to Demand That Decrease Price

blocks.md:
- Demand for lobsters in Maine, USA has been** falling** steadily in recent months
- This has resulted in a **price fall** from \$12.35 /pound on the 1st April to \$9.35 /pound on the 1st May

blocks.alt: Decrease in demand for lobsters due to a decrease in real income

blocks.md: ***Decrease in demand for lobsters due to a decrease in real income***

- In recent months, the USA has been experiencing an **increasing rate** of ***inflation***

  - Inflation lowers the **purchasing power **of money in a consumer's pocket and so effectively reduces their** *****real income***
  - With reduced real income, **fewer luxuries** are consumed
  - This led to a **decrease in demand** for lobsters from **D**<sub>**1 **</sub>**→ D**<sub>**2**</sub>
- At the **original** market clearing price of P<sub>1</sub>, a condition of** excess supply **now exists

  - The **demand** for lobsters is **less** than the **supply **
- In response, suppliers gradually **reduce prices**

  - This causes a **contraction of supply** and an **extension of demand** leading to a **new market equilibrium** at P<sub>2</sub>Q<sub>2</sub>
  - Both the **equilibrium price (P**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** & the **equilibrium quantity (Q**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** are lower than before
  - The **excess supply** in the market has been cleared

blocks.name: Real World Example: Changes to Supply That Decrease Price

blocks.text: Real World Example: Changes to Supply That Decrease Price

blocks.md: - In order to help meet their **climate targets** and lower energy costs for households, the EU is providing **subsidies** for solar panels

blocks.alt: Increase in supply of solar panels in the EU due to a per unit subsidy

blocks.md: ***Increase in supply of solar panels in the EU due to a per unit subsidy***

- To help meet its climate change targets and lower household energy bills the EU has provided a **subsidy to solar panel retailers**

  - This causes an **increase in supply **of S<sub>1 </sub>→ S<sub>2</sub>
- At the **original** market clearing price of P<sub>1</sub>, a condition of** excess supply **now exists (surplus)

  - The supply of solar panels is **greater** than the demand
- In response, sellers in the EU **lower prices**

  - This causes an **extension of demand** and a **contraction of supply** leading to a **new market equilibrium** at **P**<sub>**2**</sub>**Q**<sub>**2**</sub>
  - The **equilibrium price (P**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** is lower, and the e**quilibrium quantity (Q**<sub>**2**</sub>**)** is higher than before
  - The **excess supply** in the market has been cleared

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
In paper one, you will be frequently be asked to draw and explain effects on market, e.g the new equilibrium price and quantity after the change in the market. **Memorise the factors that shift demand and supply** - by doing so, you will save valuable time in the exam. 

**Here is a systematic process to help build your explanation:**

**Step 1:** From the scenario, identify if the change is on the **demand side** or **supply side**

**Step2:** State which way the demand or supply curve moves and use notation, e.g. S<sub>1 </sub>→ S<sub>2</sub>

**Step 3:** State the disequilibrium that now exists at the **original market price** (excess demand or excess supply)

**Step 4: **State if sellers raise or lower prices to clear the **disequilibrium**

**Step 5:** Explain the relevant **contraction** and **expansions** that occur on the demand and supply curves due to the change in price

**Step 6:** State the new market equilibrium points, e.g. P<sub>2</sub>Q<sub>2</sub>

**Step 7:** Explain the **market outcome** (is the new price/quantity higher/lower than the original?)
